newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Feb wage settlements rise average 1.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Feb wage settlements rise average 1.2 pct.

text.p: Annual wage increases in Canadian collective bargaining agreements reached in February averaged 1.2 percent, down from 1.3 percent in January, the Department of Human Resources Development said on Tuesday.
But it was slightly up from the 1996 aggregate average of 0.9 percent, the department said. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast 1.6 percent annual wage increases for February.

Wage increases are the average annual percentage increase in base rates -- the wage rate of the lowest paid classification in a bargaining unit -- over the term of the agreement in settlements negotiated during the period shown.
The 0.8 percent public sector figure was up from 0.2 percent in January and 0.5 percent for 1996 as a whole. The private sector's 2.2 percent was up from 1.9 percent in 1996.
(For more information on the settlements, contact Human Resources Development's Workplace Information Directorate, at 1-800-567-6866 or 819-997-3117.)
